lessons.title: What Is the Arctic?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe the Arctic as a very cold place with ice and snow.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at pictures of the Arctic landscape.
lessons.main_activity: Discuss where the Arctic is and what it's like there, comparing to their own local weather.
resources_needed: Arctic landscape picture cards, world map
key_questions: What is the Arctic like?
Is it hotter or colder than here?

differentiation.extension: Locate the Arctic on a world map

lessons.assessment_notes: Note geographic awareness — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Recap key Arctic facts.
lessons.home_link: Look at a world map together and find the Arctic.

lessons.title: Story Time: 'Lost and Found' by Oliver Jeffers
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe the friendship between the boy and the penguin.
lessons.starter_activity: Predict from the cover.
lessons.main_activity: Read 'Lost and Found', discussing the friendship and journey in the story.
key_questions: How do the boy and penguin become friends?
How did the penguin feel at the start vs the end?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension and emotional understanding — evidence for LIT.1.
lessons.plenary: Discuss the story's friendship theme.
lessons.home_link: Talk about a good friend and what makes them special.

lessons.title: Counting Penguins
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to count penguin counters accurately up to 10.
lessons.starter_activity: Count a group of penguin pictures together.
lessons.main_activity: Children count and sort penguin counters into groups, recording totals.
key_questions: How many penguins are there?
Can you count them again to check?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record counting accuracy — evidence for MATHS.1.
lessons.plenary: Class total penguin count.
lessons.home_link: Count objects at home together.

lessons.title: Making a Penguin Craft
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to construct a simple penguin model using craft materials.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at penguin pictures noting black/white colouring.
lessons.main_activity: Children make a penguin craft using black and white paper/card, adding an orange beak and feet.
key_questions: What colours does a penguin have?
How did you make the beak?

differentiation.extension: Cut own shapes and add detail (wings, ice)

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe fine motor and colour accuracy — evidence for EAD.1/PD.2.
lessons.plenary: Display penguin crafts together.
lessons.home_link: Draw a penguin together at home.

lessons.title: How Do Arctic Animals Stay Warm?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe one way an Arctic animal stays warm.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what keeps children warm in winter (coats).
lessons.main_activity: Discuss animal adaptations (blubber in seals/whales, thick fur in polar bears) using pictures; simple 'blubber glove' experiment if resources allow (fat/lard in a bag vs ice water).
resources_needed: Arctic animal picture cards; optional blubber glove experiment materials
key_questions: How does a polar bear stay warm?
What is blubber?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of animal adaptation — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Recap how Arctic animals stay warm.
lessons.home_link: Look up how a polar animal stays warm together.

lessons.title: Phonics: Introducing 'ch' Digraph
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to say the digraph sound 'ch' and blend words (chip, chin, chat).
lessons.starter_activity: Recap that some sounds are made of two letters.
lessons.main_activity: Introduce 'ch' digraph sound/action; blend new words.
key_questions: What sound do these two letters make together?
Can you blend ch-i-p?
lessons.assessment_notes: Begin digraph phonics tracker with 'ch'.
lessons.plenary: Practise the new digraph sound with actions.
lessons.home_link: Practise blending chip, chin, chat.

lessons.title: Sorting Arctic vs Non-Arctic Animals
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to sort animals by habitat using one criterion.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap Arctic animals learned so far.
lessons.main_activity: Children sort mixed animal picture cards into 'Arctic' and 'not Arctic' groups, counting each.
key_questions: How many Arctic animals did you find?
How did you decide?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note sorting and counting skill — evidence for MATHS.2/MATHS.1.
lessons.plenary: Class tally of both groups.
lessons.home_link: Sort toy animals into groups by habitat at home.

lessons.title: Moving Like Arctic Animals
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to move imaginatively like different Arctic animals.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss how a penguin waddles vs a seal slides.
lessons.main_activity: Children move around the space imitating penguins waddling, seals sliding, and polar bears lumbering.
key_questions: How does a penguin move?
Can you slide like a seal?

differentiation.extension: Invent an original Arctic animal movement

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe imaginative movement — evidence for EAD.2/PD.1.
lessons.plenary: Discuss favourite animal movement performed.
lessons.home_link: Act out an Arctic animal for family.

lessons.title: Floating and Sinking: Icebergs
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to observe that ice floats in water.
lessons.starter_activity: Predict whether ice will float or sink in water.
lessons.main_activity: Children test ice cubes in a water tray, observing that most of the ice stays under the surface (like an iceberg).
key_questions: Does the ice float or sink?
How much of it can you see above the water?

differentiation.extension: Predict and test other floating/sinking objects

lessons.assessment_notes: Note investigative observation — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Recap what was observed about icebergs.
lessons.home_link: Test floating and sinking objects in the bath at home.

lessons.title: Writing Arctic Animal Labels
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to attempt to write a simple label for an Arctic animal.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap Arctic animal names.
lessons.main_activity: Children draw an Arctic animal and attempt to write its name using known phonics sounds.
key_questions: Which animal are you drawing?
Can you write its name?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note writing progress — evidence for LIT.3.
lessons.plenary: Share labelled animal pictures with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Draw and label an animal together at home.

lessons.title: Number Bonds to 10 Recap with Igloo Blocks
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to recall combinations that make 10.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap number bonds to 10 from Week 16.
lessons.main_activity: Using white block 'ice bricks', children build combinations of two colours/groups that make 10, recording their bonds.
key_questions: What are the ways to make 10?
Can you find another way?
lessons.assessment_notes: Assess number bond to 10 fluency progress — evidence for MATHS.1.
lessons.plenary: Class recap of all bonds to 10 found.
lessons.home_link: Practise number bonds to 10 with any small objects at home.

lessons.title: Building an Igloo Model
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to construct a simple igloo model using materials.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at pictures of a real igloo.
lessons.main_activity: Children build a small igloo model using sugar cubes/marshmallows and icing, or white building blocks.
resources_needed: Sugar cubes/marshmallows and icing, or white blocks
key_questions: What shape is an igloo?
How did you build yours?
lessons.assessment_notes: Observe construction skill and shape understanding — evidence for EAD.1/MATHS.2.
lessons.plenary: Display igloo models together.
lessons.home_link: Build a small structure together using any materials at home.

lessons.title: Why Is the Arctic Melting? (Simple Introduction)
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to say that the Arctic ice is changing and why it's important to look after our planet.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the ice melting experiment from Week 16.
lessons.main_activity: Very simply discuss that Earth is warming and Arctic ice is melting, and that we can help by caring for our planet (recycling, saving energy).
resources_needed: Simple before/after Arctic ice picture comparison
key_questions: What is happening to the Arctic ice?
How can we help look after our planet?

differentiation.extension: Suggest a way to help the planet

lessons.assessment_notes: Note early environmental awareness — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Class list of ways to help look after the planet.
lessons.home_link: Do one thing to help look after the planet at home (recycle, turn off a light).

lessons.title: Retelling 'Lost and Found'
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retell the story's key events in sequence.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the story from Monday.
lessons.main_activity: Using picture cards, children retell the story sequence using sequencing words.
key_questions: What happened first?
What happened at the end?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note sequencing and retelling ability — evidence for LIT.1/CL.2.
lessons.plenary: One group retells to the class.
lessons.home_link: Retell the story to someone at home.

lessons.title: Symmetry with Snowflake/Ice Shapes
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify whether a shape is symmetrical.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap snowflake symmetry from Week 16.
lessons.main_activity: Children fold paper ice shapes in half to check for symmetry, sorting symmetrical and non-symmetrical examples.
key_questions: Is this shape symmetrical?
How do you know?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note early symmetry understanding — evidence for MATHS.2.
lessons.plenary: Class recap of symmetrical shapes found.
lessons.home_link: Look for symmetrical shapes/objects at home.

lessons.title: Arctic Animals Song and Dance
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to sing an Arctic-themed song with matching actions.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap Arctic animal movements from Tuesday.
lessons.main_activity: Learn a simple Arctic animal song with actions (waddle like a penguin, swim like a seal), performing with confidence.
key_questions: What action goes with this line?
Which animal do you like moving as most?

differentiation.extension: Suggest and lead a new action

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe participation and expressive movement — evidence for EAD.2.
lessons.plenary: Perform the song once more.
lessons.home_link: Sing the Arctic song for family.

lessons.title: Arctic Animals Recap Display
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key facts about the Arctic and its animals learned this week.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's UTW learning.
lessons.main_activity: Contribute to a class 'Arctic Animals' display summarising habitat, adaptation, and environmental care learning.
key_questions: What have we learned about the Arctic?
What was most interesting?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of the week's learning — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Unveil the finished display.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about the Arctic with your family.

lessons.title: Phonics Review: Recap Including 'ch'
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read words including the 'ch' digraph.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap 'ch' and other sounds learned.
lessons.main_activity: Phonics stations: word-building with 'ch', CVC and digraph reading cards, simple sentence reading.
key_questions: Can you build and read this word?
Can you read this sentence?

differentiation.support: Build/read simple digraph words with support

lessons.assessment_notes: Update phonics tracker for 'ch' digraph progress.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate the new digraph learned this week.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading words with 'ch' over the weekend.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Counting, Sorting, Symmetry
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply counting, sorting, and symmetry skills learned this week.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's maths vocabulary.
lessons.main_activity: Rotate through 3 stations: counting penguins, sorting Arctic/non-Arctic animals, symmetry checking.
key_questions: How many is this?
Which group does this belong to?
Is this symmetrical?
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 17 maths observations.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining all three skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising sorting and symmetry over the weekend.

lessons.title: Arctic Animals Celebration Performance
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to combine movement, song, and craft in a short class performance.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap all elements learned this week.
lessons.main_activity: Whole-class performance combining Arctic animal movements and the song, with penguin/igloo craft displayed.
resources_needed: Craft from the week, music player
key_questions: What was your favourite part of this week?
How did it feel to perform?
lessons.assessment_notes: Observe confidence and enjoyment — evidence for EAD.2.
lessons.plenary: Round of applause; recap the Arctic animals week.
lessons.home_link: Perform an Arctic animal movement for family this weekend.
